project.name: linux-net-core-devmem
project.description: TCP devmem subsystem of the Linux kernel (net/core). Page-pool allocator with a memory-provider abstraction that allows network RX to land directly into dmabuf-backed device memory (e.g., GPU memory), enabling zero-copy receive. Includes netlink API (netdev-genl) for binding dmabufs to RX queues.

nodes.name: devmem.c
nodes.summary: Implements the TCP devmem subsystem that binds userspace dmabufs to netdev RX queues, manages net_iov chunks carved from device memory, and provides the page_pool memory_provider_ops used to land zero-copy RX traffic directly into GPU/device memory.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses gen_pool for sub-page chunk allocation over dmabuf-mapped sg_table, percpu_ref for binding lifetime, and xarray to track per-binding rxq attachments.

nodes.name: devmem.h
nodes.summary: Public header for the devmem subsystem defining net_devmem_dmabuf_binding, dmabuf_genpool_chunk_owner, and inline accessors for net_iov ownership, virtual address translation, and binding refcount management.
nodes.languageNotes: Header provides CONFIG_NET_DEVMEM-gated stubs so callers compile without devmem support; inline helpers wrap percpu_ref get/put for binding lifetime.

nodes.name: mp_dmabuf_devmem.h
nodes.summary: Tiny header that declares the dmabuf devmem memory_provider entry points (init, alloc_netmems, destroy, release_page) consumed by page_pool to plug devmem in as an alternative netmem source.

nodes.name: netdev-genl.c
nodes.summary: Generic netlink command handlers for the netdev family covering device/NAPI/queue introspection, per-queue stats dumps, and the bind-RX/bind-TX/queue-create commands that expose devmem dmabuf binding to userspace.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of genlmsg_iput/nla_put_* netlink serialization helpers and netdev_dump_ctx pagination state for dumpit callbacks.

nodes.name: __net_devmem_dmabuf_binding_free
nodes.summary: Workqueue handler that tears down a devmem binding by freeing all gen_pool chunks, unmapping/detaching the dmabuf, destroying the xarray, and releasing the percpu_ref state.

nodes.name: net_devmem_unbind_dmabuf
nodes.summary: Tears down a dmabuf-to-RX-queue binding by erasing xarray entries, synchronizing the net, closing each affected RX queue via netif_mp_close_rxq, and killing the percpu_ref so deferred free can run.

nodes.name: net_devmem_bind_dmabuf_to_queue
nodes.summary: Installs a devmem binding on a specific RX queue index by calling netif_mp_open_rxq with the dmabuf memory-provider params and tracking the queue in the binding's xarray for later teardown.

nodes.name: mp_dmabuf_devmem_init
nodes.summary: page_pool memory-provider init callback: validates the pool is configured for devmem (DMA_FROM_DEVICE, order 0, no DMA mapping) and takes a reference on the dmabuf binding for the pool's lifetime.

nodes.name: mp_dmabuf_devmem_alloc_netmems
nodes.summary: page_pool allocation callback that draws a net_iov chunk from the binding's gen_pool, converts it to a netmem, attaches page_pool metadata, and emits the page-pool hold tracepoint.

nodes.name: mp_dmabuf_devmem_release_page
nodes.summary: page_pool release callback that asserts the netmem is a net_iov with a zero refcount, clears its page_pool metadata, and returns the chunk back to the dmabuf gen_pool for reuse.

nodes.name: mp_dmabuf_devmem_uninstall
nodes.summary: Tears down the per-queue memory-provider state: removes this rxq from every binding's xarray and clears the rxq's mp_params under the mp_mutex with proper RCU/exclusive-writer assertions.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_dev_fill
nodes.summary: Serializes per-netdev attributes (ifindex, xdp features, xdp-zc/rx-metadata features, xsk_features) into a genl message for NETDEV_CMD_DEV_GET responses and notifications.

nodes.name: netdev_genl_dev_notify
nodes.summary: Broadcasts NETDEV_CMD_DEV_ADD/DEL_NTF multicast notifications when a netdev is registered or unregistered so userspace listeners can stay in sync.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_dev_get_doit
nodes.summary: Doit handler for NETDEV_CMD_DEV_GET: validates the ifindex attribute, looks up and locks the netdev, and replies with its netdev_nl_dev_fill encoding.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_dev_get_dumpit
nodes.summary: Dumpit handler that iterates every netdev in the requesting netns and fills one device record per skb element using netdev_nl_dev_fill.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_napi_fill_one
nodes.summary: Encodes a single napi_struct's id, owning ifindex, IRQ number, threading state, defer-hard-irqs, suspend timeout, and GRO flush timeout into a genl message.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_napi_get_doit
nodes.summary: Doit handler for NETDEV_CMD_NAPI_GET that resolves a napi_id, takes the netdev lock, and replies with the corresponding NAPI's serialized attributes.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_napi_dump_one
nodes.summary: Helper that walks one netdev's NAPI list and emits a NAPI record per valid napi_id while resuming from the dump context's napi_id cursor.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_napi_get_dumpit
nodes.summary: Dumpit handler that iterates NAPIs across all netdevs (or a single requested ifindex) using netdev_nl_napi_dump_one.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_napi_set_config
nodes.summary: Applies user-supplied NAPI tuning attributes (threaded mode, defer-hard-irqs, irq-suspend-timeout, gro-flush-timeout) onto the target napi_struct.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_napi_set_doit
nodes.summary: Doit handler for NETDEV_CMD_NAPI_SET that resolves the napi_id, takes the netdev lock, and delegates to netdev_nl_napi_set_config.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_queue_fill_lease
nodes.summary: Fills the nested 'lease' attribute for a queue, reporting the leasee netns (with nsid translation) and the borrowing ifindex when the rxq has been leased out.

nodes.name: __netdev_nl_queue_fill_mp
nodes.summary: Inner helper that delegates to the memory-provider's nl_fill op (e.g., mp_dmabuf_devmem_nl_fill) to encode provider-specific attributes for an RX queue.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_queue_fill_mp
nodes.summary: Wraps __netdev_nl_queue_fill_mp with the right locking depending on whether the queue is leased, taking netdev_lock when querying the local netdev's MP state.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_queue_fill_one
nodes.summary: Encodes a single queue (RX or TX) into a genl message including its id, type, NAPI id, and either lease + memory-provider info for RX or an empty XSK nest for TX.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_queue_get_doit
nodes.summary: Doit handler for NETDEV_CMD_QUEUE_GET that validates the ifindex/id/type triple and replies with that single queue's serialized state.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_queue_dump_one
nodes.summary: Iterates real_num_rx_queues and real_num_tx_queues for one netdev, resuming from the dump context cursor and emitting one queue record per index.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_queue_get_dumpit
nodes.summary: Dumpit handler that walks queues across all netdevs (or a single requested ifindex), pausing/resuming on the netdev_dump_ctx cursor.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_stats_write_rx
nodes.summary: Emits the full set of per-queue RX counters (packets, bytes, alloc fails, hw drops, csum errors, etc.) using netdev_stat_put.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_stats_write_tx
nodes.summary: Emits the full set of per-queue TX counters (packets, bytes, drops, wake/stops, hw drops, csum issues) using netdev_stat_put.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_stats_queue
nodes.summary: Reads per-queue rx or tx stats via the driver's get_queue_stats_* op and serializes them as a netlink record keyed by ifindex and queue id.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_stats_by_queue
nodes.summary: Per-queue stats dump scope that iterates all RX then TX queues for one netdev, resuming from the dump context cursor.

nodes.name: netdev_stat_queue_sum
nodes.summary: Sums per-queue rx and tx stats across an index range using the driver's get_queue_stats callbacks into the provided rollup structures.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_stats_by_netdev
nodes.summary: Per-netdev stats dump scope that aggregates queue stats into device-level rx/tx totals and adds the unread tail from the driver's base device counters.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_qstats_get_dump_one
nodes.summary: Per-netdev dispatcher for qstats dumps that selects between per-netdev and per-queue stat-emission paths based on the requested scope.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_qstats_get_dumpit
nodes.summary: Top-level dumpit for NETDEV_CMD_QSTATS_GET that parses the scope attribute and iterates netdevs invoking netdev_nl_qstats_get_dump_one.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_read_rxq_bitmap
nodes.summary: Parses a nested NETDEV_A_DMABUF_QUEUES attribute list into a bitmap of RX queue indices, validating each id and rejecting duplicates.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_bind_rx_doit
nodes.summary: Userspace entry point for NETDEV_CMD_BIND_RX that resolves the dmabuf fd, allocates a net_devmem binding, attaches it to every requested RX queue, and returns the new binding id (rolling back on partial failure).

nodes.name: netdev_nl_bind_tx_doit
nodes.summary: Userspace entry point for NETDEV_CMD_BIND_TX that creates a TX-side devmem binding for the requesting socket so it can send from dmabuf memory.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_queue_create_doit
nodes.summary: Handler for NETDEV_CMD_QUEUE_CREATE that provisions a new queue (optionally leasing from a peer netns, attaching a devmem binding, and configuring NAPI) and returns the created queue id.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_sock_priv_destroy
nodes.summary: Per-genl-socket cleanup that walks every devmem binding owned by the closing socket and triggers unbind to release dmabuf resources.

nodes.name: netdev_genl_netdevice_event
nodes.summary: Notifier callback that emits NETDEV_CMD_DEV_ADD/DEL_NTF multicast messages on NETDEV_REGISTER/UNREGISTER events.

nodes.name: netdev_genl_init
nodes.summary: Subsys init that registers the netdev generic-netlink family and installs the netdevice notifier for ADD/DEL notifications.

nodes.name: memory_provider_ops
nodes.summary: Definition of the dmabuf_devmem_ops memory_provider_ops vtable wiring init/alloc_netmems/destroy/release_netmem/nl_fill/uninstall callbacks consumed by page_pool.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_dump_ctx
nodes.summary: Pagination cursor struct used by netdev genl dumpit callbacks to remember the next ifindex, rxq, txq, and napi_id to emit across multi-skb dumps.

nodes.name: netdev_rx_queue.c
nodes.summary: Implements atomic RX queue reconfiguration and memory provider install/uninstall on a single queue, including the lease mechanism that maps a virtual RX queue onto a physical one for devmem binding.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses ndo_queue_* device ops to swap a queue's memory provider live with rollback paths; relies on READ_ONCE/WRITE_ONCE and netdev_assert_locked for concurrency.

nodes.name: page_pool_priv.h
nodes.summary: Private header shared between page_pool.c, page_pool_user.c, and devmem.c; declares the memory_provider_ops interface and internal helpers for DMA address handling on netmem.

nodes.name: page_pool_user.c
nodes.summary: Netlink-side reporting and lifecycle tracking for page_pools: implements netdev-genl get/dump handlers, stats serialization, pool registry (XArray + hlist), and netdevice notifier for unregister-time cleanup.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of nla_put_* serialization helpers, XArray for pool ID allocation, and hlist chains anchored on net_device for per-device pool tracking.

nodes.name: netdev_rx_queue_reconfig
nodes.summary: Core atomic queue reconfiguration: allocates new queue memory, stops the old queue, starts the new one, and swaps configs with full rollback on failure at each step.

nodes.name: netdev_rx_queue_restart
nodes.summary: Public entry point that restarts an RX queue by capturing the current config and calling netdev_rx_queue_reconfig with identical old/new configs.

nodes.name: __netif_mp_open_rxq
nodes.summary: Installs a memory provider on an RX queue: validates queue ops are present, checks XDP/MP compatibility, builds the new queue config with the provider parameters, and triggers reconfig.

nodes.name: netif_mp_open_rxq
nodes.summary: Wrapper around __netif_mp_open_rxq that handles RX queue lease lookup, ops-lock acquisition, and validates the queue index before installing a memory provider.

nodes.name: __netif_mp_close_rxq
nodes.summary: Removes the memory provider from an RX queue by clearing the mp_params field in the queue config and triggering a reconfig back to default page allocation.

nodes.name: netif_mp_close_rxq
nodes.summary: Public memory provider close wrapper that resolves the leased physical queue and acquires the netdev ops lock around __netif_mp_close_rxq.

nodes.name: netif_rxq_cleanup_unlease
nodes.summary: Tears down a leased RX queue pairing: uninstalls any installed memory provider and closes the queue, used when a virtual RX queue is released from its physical lessor.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_page_pool_get_do
nodes.summary: Shared do-handler helper that looks up a page_pool by ID in the XArray, validates net namespace, and delegates serialization to a caller-provided fill callback.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_page_pool_get_dump
nodes.summary: Shared dump iterator that walks all netdevs (or one by ifindex) and emits one netlink message per page_pool via the provided fill callback, supporting resume across calls.

nodes.name: page_pool_nl_stats_fill
nodes.summary: Serializes a page_pool's complete stats counters (alloc, recycle, refill) into a nested netlink attribute structure for the stats-get response.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_page_pool_stats_get_doit
nodes.summary: Top-level netlink do-handler for NETDEV_CMD_PAGE_POOL_STATS_GET: parses the nested page-pool info attribute and invokes the shared get-do helper with the stats fill callback.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_page_pool_stats_get_dumpit
nodes.summary: Netlink dumpit entry for page-pool stats: parses optional ifindex filter and delegates to the shared dump iterator with the stats fill callback.

nodes.name: page_pool_nl_fill
nodes.summary: Serializes a page_pool's identity (id, ifindex, napi-id, inflight, dmabuf binding, detach-time) into a netlink message for the page-pool get/dump command.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_page_pool_event
nodes.summary: Broadcasts a page_pool lifecycle event (add/del/change) as a netlink notification to multicast listeners in the appropriate net namespace.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_page_pool_get_doit
nodes.summary: Top-level netlink do-handler for NETDEV_CMD_PAGE_POOL_GET that parses the requested page-pool ID and dispatches to the shared get-do helper with the identity fill callback.

nodes.name: netdev_nl_page_pool_get_dumpit
nodes.summary: Netlink dumpit entry for listing all page_pools, delegating to the shared dump iterator with the identity fill callback.

nodes.name: page_pool_list
nodes.summary: Registers a newly created page_pool in the global XArray ID registry and per-netdev hlist, then emits an add notification; called from page_pool_create.

nodes.name: page_pool_detached
nodes.summary: Marks a page_pool as detached from its driver (records boottime) and emits a change notification, called during page_pool_destroy.

nodes.name: page_pool_unlist
nodes.summary: Removes a page_pool from the global XArray and per-device hlist, emitting a del notification; called when the pool is fully released.

nodes.name: page_pool_check_memory_provider
nodes.summary: Verifies that the driver re-created a page_pool on the expected RX queue with the configured memory provider after a queue restart, returning -ENODATA if not found.

nodes.name: page_pool_unreg_netdev_wipe
nodes.summary: On netdev unregister with no surviving pools, removes all per-device page_pool entries from the hlist without sending events.

nodes.name: page_pool_unreg_netdev
nodes.summary: Handles netdev unregister when pools remain alive: orphans them by reassigning their hlist to the loopback netdev so stats/notifications still resolve.

nodes.name: page_pool_netdevice_event
nodes.summary: Netdevice notifier callback that routes NETDEV_UNREGISTER events to either the wipe or orphan path depending on whether any pools survive.

nodes.name: netmem_priv.h
nodes.summary: Private inline helpers that read and mutate page_pool bookkeeping fields on a netmem_ref (the tagged-pointer abstraction over struct page or net_iov), including pp_magic, the page_pool back-pointer, DMA address and DMA index.
nodes.languageNotes: All symbols are static inline helpers; netmem_is_pp() relies on shared page_type offset between struct page and net_iov — flagged in-source with an XXX as a layout assumption.

nodes.name: page_pool.c
nodes.summary: Core page_pool allocator and recycler for network RX buffers, with a memory_provider_ops indirection that lets a custom provider (e.g., the devmem dmabuf provider) supply netmems backed by net_iov slices of GPU/device memory.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of EXPORT_SYMBOL and per-CPU ptr_ring for the recycle path; the net_mp_niov_* helpers form the contract used by memory providers to wire net_iov instances into the pool.

nodes.name: page_pool_init
nodes.summary: Validates pool parameters, allocates per-CPU recycle ring, picks the right memory provider (default or custom mp_ops such as dmabuf devmem), and binds DMA mapping/sync flags.

nodes.name: page_pool_uninit
nodes.summary: Tears down internal page_pool state allocated by page_pool_init, including the recycle ring and DMA index xarray.

nodes.name: page_pool_refill_alloc_cache
nodes.summary: Refills the per-pool fast-path allocation cache by draining the recycle ptr_ring, honoring NUMA-node affinity to avoid cross-node netmems.

nodes.name: __page_pool_get_cached
nodes.summary: Returns a cached netmem from the lockless alloc cache, refilling from the recycle ring on miss.

nodes.name: __page_pool_dma_sync_for_device
nodes.summary: Performs an explicit dma_sync_single_range_for_device on the netmem's DMA mapping, used on the RX recycle path when sync-for-device is required.

nodes.name: page_pool_dma_sync_for_device
nodes.summary: Conditional wrapper that invokes __page_pool_dma_sync_for_device only when the pool is configured to manage DMA sync.

nodes.name: page_pool_register_dma_index
nodes.summary: Allocates an xarray slot for a netmem so the pool can later look up the DMA mapping for unmap on release; encodes the index into pp_magic.

nodes.name: page_pool_release_dma_index
nodes.summary: Looks up the DMA index encoded in pp_magic and releases the xarray slot; complements page_pool_register_dma_index.

nodes.name: page_pool_dma_map
nodes.summary: Maps a freshly allocated netmem for device DMA, stashing the DMA address back into the netmem's nmdesc and registering a DMA index if needed.

nodes.name: __page_pool_alloc_netmems_slow
nodes.summary: Slow-path bulk allocator that requests a batch of pages from the buddy/page allocator, DMA-maps them, and stages them into the recycle ring as netmems.

nodes.name: page_pool_alloc_netmems
nodes.summary: Public entry point that returns a netmem, dispatching to the custom memory_provider's alloc_netmems hook when configured (devmem dmabuf path) or to the default fast/slow path otherwise.

nodes.name: page_pool_inflight
nodes.summary: Returns the number of netmems still held by the network stack (allocated minus released), used by destroy/scrub paths to decide whether to defer teardown.

nodes.name: page_pool_set_pp_info
nodes.summary: Stamps a netmem with the owning page_pool back-pointer and pp_magic value so the recycle path can identify and route it back to this pool; called by both default and devmem providers.

nodes.name: page_pool_clear_pp_info
nodes.summary: Clears pp_magic and the page_pool back-pointer on a netmem when it is being released back to its underlying allocator (page allocator or devmem provider).

nodes.name: __page_pool_release_netmem_dma
nodes.summary: Unmaps a netmem's DMA mapping and releases its DMA-index xarray slot when the netmem leaves the pool for good.

nodes.name: page_pool_return_netmem
nodes.summary: Returns a netmem to its underlying allocator, dispatching to mp_ops->release_netmem for devmem-backed netmems or to the default page-allocator release path.

nodes.name: page_pool_recycle_in_ring
nodes.summary: Pushes a netmem onto the per-pool ptr_ring so any CPU can later pull it from the recycle path.

nodes.name: page_pool_recycle_in_cache
nodes.summary: Stashes a netmem into the per-pool lockless alloc cache (NAPI-local fast path) when there is room.

nodes.name: __page_pool_put_page
nodes.summary: Core recycle decision: if the netmem can be recycled, optionally sync-for-device, then try the NAPI-local cache or the ptr_ring; otherwise release it to its underlying allocator.

nodes.name: page_pool_napi_local
nodes.summary: Returns true if the calling context is the NAPI instance that owns the pool, which enables the lockless cache recycle fast path.

nodes.name: page_pool_put_unrefed_netmem
nodes.summary: Public netmem-returning entry point: callers that already dropped their refcount funnel through __page_pool_put_page to recycle or release.

nodes.name: page_pool_recycle_ring_bulk
nodes.summary: Bulk variant that pushes an array of netmems into the ptr_ring under a single producer lock and releases any leftovers via the slow path.

nodes.name: page_pool_put_netmem_bulk
nodes.summary: Public bulk recycle API: groups netmems by owning pool, then for each pool either drops them into the NAPI cache, the ptr_ring, or releases them.

nodes.name: page_pool_drain_frag
nodes.summary: Drops the page-pool's reference on a fragmented netmem and either recycles or releases it once no fragments remain.

nodes.name: page_pool_free_frag
nodes.summary: Releases the current frag-netmem cached on the pool, used when the pool itself is being torn down.

nodes.name: page_pool_alloc_frag_netmem
nodes.summary: Public sub-page fragment allocator that hands out a slice of a shared netmem, allocating a fresh one and resetting the offset when the current one is exhausted.

nodes.name: page_pool_empty_ring
nodes.summary: Drains the recycle ptr_ring, returning each netmem to its underlying allocator; part of pool teardown.

nodes.name: __page_pool_destroy
nodes.summary: Final teardown helper that destroys the user-visible page_pool object once all inflight netmems have been returned.

nodes.name: page_pool_empty_alloc_cache_once
nodes.summary: One-shot drain of the lockless alloc cache, releasing each cached netmem to its underlying allocator.

nodes.name: page_pool_scrub
nodes.summary: Detaches the pool from its memory provider (e.g., devmem dmabuf) and drains caches before destruction; safe to call repeatedly.

nodes.name: page_pool_release
nodes.summary: Releases all in-flight netmems still tracked by the pool and frees the pool itself once the inflight count reaches zero.

nodes.name: page_pool_release_retry
nodes.summary: Delayed workqueue handler that retries page_pool_release periodically until all inflight netmems are returned, with a warning if the pool stalls.

nodes.name: page_pool_enable_direct_recycling
nodes.summary: Binds the pool to a NAPI instance so XDP / RX paths can recycle netmems directly into the lockless cache without ring contention.

nodes.name: page_pool_disable_direct_recycling
nodes.summary: Unbinds the pool from its NAPI instance, ensuring no new direct-cache recycles happen before tearing down.

nodes.name: page_pool_destroy
nodes.summary: Public teardown API: disables direct recycling, scrubs caches and memory provider, then schedules a delayed release until inflight is drained.

nodes.name: page_pool_update_nid
nodes.summary: Updates the pool's NUMA node affinity and drains the alloc cache so subsequent allocations land on the new node.

nodes.name: net_mp_niov_set_dma_addr
nodes.summary: Memory-provider helper that stashes a pre-computed DMA address into a net_iov so the page_pool fast path can use it without re-mapping.

nodes.name: net_mp_niov_set_page_pool
nodes.summary: Memory-provider helper that wires a net_iov (devmem slice) into a page_pool, stamping pp/pp_magic so recycle paths route it back correctly.

nodes.name: net_mp_niov_clear_page_pool
nodes.summary: Memory-provider helper that unbinds a net_iov from its page_pool, used when the dmabuf binding is being torn down.

nodes.name: skbuff.c
nodes.summary: Master socket-buffer allocator/destructor, fragment manipulator, and zerocopy/timestamping engine; devmem-aware paths route page-pool/dmabuf netmems through __get_netmem/__put_netmem and the skb_pp_cow/skb_zcopy code paths.
nodes.languageNotes: Very large translation unit; devmem touch-points are concentrated in __get_netmem/__put_netmem, skb_pp_cow_data, skb_pp_frag_ref and the ubuf_info / msg_zerocopy callbacks — most other helpers are general SKB infrastructure.

nodes.name: __get_netmem
nodes.summary: Per-fragment netmem get for SKBs: if the netmem is a devmem net_iov, takes a devmem reference so the dmabuf binding stays alive while the skb holds the fragment.

nodes.name: __put_netmem
nodes.summary: Per-fragment netmem put for SKBs: drops the devmem reference taken by __get_netmem when an skb fragment backed by a net_iov is released.

nodes.name: skb_pp_cow_data
nodes.summary: Copy-on-write helper that linearizes an SKB whose fragments may be unreadable (devmem) into freshly allocated page-pool pages so XDP and other in-kernel consumers can touch the payload.

nodes.name: skb_cow_data_for_xdp
nodes.summary: Wrapper that triggers skb_pp_cow_data when XDP needs a readable, linearized buffer, e.g., when the original frags are devmem-backed.

nodes.name: skb_pp_frag_ref
nodes.summary: Bumps refcount on each netmem fragment of a page-pool-backed skb, branching into devmem net_iov refcounting when the netmem is devmem.

nodes.name: skb_release_data
nodes.summary: Releases the shared data area of an skb, dropping refs on every page/netmem fragment (including devmem net_iovs via __put_netmem) before freeing head data.

nodes.name: skb_free_head
nodes.summary: Frees an skb's head buffer, routing through the page_pool recycle path when the head came from a page_pool.

nodes.name: kfree_skbmem
nodes.summary: Returns the skb struct itself to its origin slab/cache after data has been released.

nodes.name: skb_release_head_state
nodes.summary: Drops references held in the skb head (destructor, secpath, nf_conntrack, etc.) before the buffer is freed.

nodes.name: __kfree_skb
nodes.summary: Internal free: releases head state, data, and the skb struct itself.

nodes.name: __sk_skb_reason_drop
nodes.summary: Slow-path SKB drop that emits a tracepoint with the supplied SKB_DROP_REASON before freeing.

nodes.name: sk_skb_reason_drop
nodes.summary: Public per-socket skb drop helper that annotates the drop with a reason.

nodes.name: kfree_skb_add_bulk
nodes.summary: Helper that accumulates skbs into a bulk-free array, flushing when the array is full.

nodes.name: kfree_skb_list_reason
nodes.summary: Bulk-frees an entire skb list with a single drop reason and tracepoint per skb.

nodes.name: skb_dump
nodes.summary: Diagnostic helper that pretty-prints an skb's headers, metadata, and (optionally) payload to the kernel log.

nodes.name: skb_tx_error
nodes.summary: Notifies any attached zerocopy callback that the buffer hit a TX error path.

nodes.name: __consume_stateless_skb
nodes.summary: Frees a stateless RX skb after the data has been consumed (no destructor needed).

nodes.name: napi_skb_cache_put
nodes.summary: Pushes a freed skb onto the per-NAPI skb cache for reuse, flushing back to the slab when the cache is full.

nodes.name: __napi_kfree_skb
nodes.summary: NAPI-context free that routes through the per-NAPI skb cache.

nodes.name: napi_skb_free_stolen_head
nodes.summary: Frees an skb whose head data was stolen by a coalescer, recycling the shell back into the NAPI cache.

nodes.name: napi_consume_skb
nodes.summary: Releases an skb after a budgeted NAPI poll, preferring the NAPI per-CPU cache and falling back to the slab.

nodes.name: __copy_skb_header

nodes.name: sock.c
nodes.summary: Generic socket-layer infrastructure for the Linux kernel: socket allocation, option dispatch (setsockopt/getsockopt), control-message handling, memory accounting, and protocol registration. For devmem, this file owns the SO_DEVMEM_DONTNEED socket option (token-return path) and the SCM_DEVMEM_DMABUF cmsg parsing that lets userspace tag TX skbs with a dmabuf binding id.
nodes.languageNotes: Very large translation unit (4573 lines) acting as the central socket dispatcher. The devmem-specific code is gated by CONFIG_PAGE_POOL and lives in a small island around sock_devmem_dontneed plus a SCM_DEVMEM_DMABUF case in __sock_cmsg_send; the surrounding file is generic socket infrastructure unrelated to devmem.

nodes.name: sock_devmem_dontneed
nodes.summary: Implements the SO_DEVMEM_DONTNEED socket option: userspace passes an array of dmabuf_token ranges (token_start, token_count) describing previously surfaced devmem fragments, and this function erases the matching netmem refs from sk->sk_user_frags and returns them to the page pool via napi_pp_put_page. TCP-only; bounded by MAX_DONTNEED_TOKENS (128) and MAX_DONTNEED_FRAGS (1024) to cap per-syscall work. Returns the number of frags successfully released.

nodes.name: __sock_cmsg_send
nodes.summary: Parses a single SOL_SOCKET-level ancillary control message attached to sendmsg() and folds it into a sockcm_cookie. For devmem it handles SCM_DEVMEM_DMABUF, which lets userspace stamp the outgoing skb with a dmabuf binding id (sockc->dmabuf_id) so TX zero-copy can target device memory; also handles SO_MARK, SO_TIMESTAMPING, TS_OPT_ID, SO_TXTIME, SO_PRIORITY, SCM_TS_OPT_ID, SCM_RIGHTS, SCM_CREDENTIALS.

nodes.name: sk_setsockopt
nodes.summary: Central dispatcher for SOL_SOCKET-level setsockopt requests. Relevant to devmem because the SO_DEVMEM_DONTNEED case (line 1299) routes directly to sock_devmem_dontneed, exposing the token-return path to userspace. Otherwise handles the full menu of generic socket options (rcvbuf, sndbuf, timestamps, BPF filter attach, marks, busy poll, etc.).

nodes.name: sk_getsockopt
nodes.summary: Companion dispatcher for SOL_SOCKET-level getsockopt; returns runtime socket state (buffers, timestamps, peer creds, memory info, BPF, busy poll, etc.). No devmem-specific cases live here today, but it is the symmetric option-read surface that future devmem socket-options would extend.

nodes.name: sock_init_data_uid
nodes.summary: Initializes a freshly allocated struct sock with default queues, callbacks, sysctl-derived buffer sizes, and rcu protected fields. Devmem reuses the standard sk->sk_user_frags xarray that is initialized as part of socket setup elsewhere; this routine is the canonical sk bring-up path.

nodes.name: __sk_destruct
nodes.summary: Final socket destructor invoked after the last reference is dropped: drains queues, releases filter, peer creds, dst entries and frees the sk via its protocol allocator. Relevant to devmem because any tokens still pinned in sk->sk_user_frags at close time must already have been returned (TCP's sock destructor handles outstanding devmem cleanup before this point).

nodes.name: __sk_mem_raise_allocated
nodes.summary: Core memory-accounting routine: charges 'amt' protocol-level memory pages against the socket and its memcg, applying pressure thresholds. Devmem RX bypasses this for the data payload itself (pages live in dmabuf-backed page-pool), but skb head/metadata still flows through this accounting.

nodes.name: proto_register
nodes.summary: Registers a struct proto (allocates per-proto slab caches and twsk/rsk caches, links into proto_list, exposes /proc entries). Indirect devmem relevance: TCP, the only protocol that consumes devmem today, is registered through this entry point.

nodes.name: sock_struct_check
nodes.summary: Build-time BUILD_BUG_ON checks asserting that performance-critical struct sock fields land in the expected cachelines. Pure infrastructure with no devmem coupling.

layers.name: Userspace API Surface
layers.description: Netlink command handlers and socket-option dispatch that expose devmem dmabuf binding, page_pool stats, and the SO_DEVMEM_DONTNEED / SCM_DEVMEM_DMABUF interfaces to userspace.

layers.name: Devmem Binding Core
layers.description: Implementation of the dmabuf-to-RX-queue binding: net_iov chunk management, the dmabuf memory_provider_ops, and atomic per-queue memory-provider install/uninstall used to wire device memory into a netdev RX queue.

layers.name: Page-Pool & Netmem Core
layers.description: Generic page_pool RX-buffer allocator plus the netmem tagged-pointer abstraction; defines the memory_provider_ops indirection that the devmem provider plugs into to back netmems with net_iov slices of device memory.

layers.name: SKB Data-Path Integration
layers.description: Socket-buffer allocator and fragment/zerocopy engine where page-pool and dmabuf-backed netmems are produced and consumed via __get_netmem/__put_netmem and the skb_pp_cow / skb_zcopy paths.

tour.title: Core Types & Memory Provider ABI
tour.description: Begin with the two header files that define the devmem world. devmem.h declares net_devmem_dmabuf_binding (the per-dmabuf binding object), dmabuf_genpool_chunk_owner (which carves dmabuf SG entries into sub-page chunks), and the inline helpers that translate a net_iov back to its owning binding and virtual address. mp_dmabuf_devmem.h declares the four memory_provider_ops callbacks (init, alloc_netmems, destroy, release_netmem) that page_pool will invoke. Together these establish the central abstraction the rest of the subsystem revolves around: a pluggable memory provider that backs page_pool netmems with slices of device memory.
tour.languageLesson: The Linux kernel uses ops-struct indirection (here memory_provider_ops) as its primary form of polymorphism in C. A provider implementation fills in function pointers; page_pool calls them generically, never knowing whether memory comes from regular pages or a dmabuf.

tour.title: netmem: The Tagged-Pointer Abstraction
tour.description: Before any allocator code, understand the netmem_ref pointer type. netmem_priv.h defines the bit-tagging scheme that lets a single netmem_ref hold either a struct page or a net_iov (devmem slice), along with the pp_magic, back-pointer and DMA bookkeeping that page_pool relies on. This is the unifying type that makes the rest of the kernel network stack indifferent to whether RX data lives in host RAM or GPU memory.
tour.languageLesson: Tagged pointers exploit alignment guarantees: because struct page and net_iov are always aligned, the low bits of a pointer are free to encode the discriminant. NET_IOV_ASSERTS verifies layout compatibility so the two variants can share helpers like page_to_pfn-style accessors.

tour.title: Userspace Entry: NETDEV_CMD_BIND_RX
tour.description: The data flow begins in userspace, which sends a generic-netlink BIND_RX command. netdev_nl_bind_rx_doit parses the netlink message, resolves the dmabuf fd, allocates a binding object, then iterates the requested queue indices, calling into the devmem core for each one. This is the boundary where an opaque file descriptor turns into a kernel object that owns device memory.
tour.languageLesson: generic netlink (genl) is the kernel's primary modern userspace control-plane RPC. Commands are dispatched via a per-family ops table; doit handlers run synchronously while dumpit handlers stream results in chunks for list/get-all operations.

tour.title: Binding a dmabuf to an RX Queue
tour.description: net_devmem_bind_dmabuf_to_queue is the heart of the binding flow. Building on Step 3, it takes the binding object (which has already pinned the dmabuf and carved it into net_iov chunks via gen_pool), then installs the devmem memory_provider_ops on a specific RX queue by calling into the queue-restart machinery. After this returns, the NIC's RX descriptors on that queue will be filled with addresses from device memory.
tour.languageLesson: gen_pool is the kernel's general-purpose allocator for sub-page chunks carved out of an arbitrary region. devmem uses it to hand out fixed-size net_iov slices from a dmabuf's scatter-gather table without needing a struct page for each slice.

tour.title: Atomically Swapping the Memory Provider
tour.description: An RX queue may be live with traffic when a binding is installed, so the memory provider must be swapped without dropping packets. netdev_rx_queue_restart captures the current queue config, asks the driver to stop the queue, swaps the page_pool's memory provider, then asks the driver to restart. This is the choreography that makes online dmabuf binding possible.
tour.languageLesson: The kernel pattern of pause-mutate-resume is common for hot-path reconfiguration: rather than locking the data path on every packet, the control path briefly quiesces it. Drivers expose ndo_queue_mem_alloc / ndo_queue_start hooks so generic code can drive the dance.

tour.title: page_pool Dispatches to the Provider
tour.description: With the binding installed, every NIC RX refill flows through page_pool_alloc_netmems. When a custom memory_provider is configured on the pool, allocation is delegated to mp->ops->alloc_netmems, which lands in mp_dmabuf_devmem_alloc_netmems. That callback pulls a net_iov out of the binding's gen_pool and wraps it in a netmem_ref. This is where the data path actually consumes device memory instead of host pages.
tour.languageLesson: Hot-path indirection in the kernel is typically gated by a branch predictor friendly check (e.g., likely(!pool->mp_ops)) so the common no-provider case has near-zero overhead while still allowing pluggable providers.

tour.title: Devmem-Aware SKB Fragments
tour.description: Once the NIC writes into device memory, the kernel wraps those netmems in an SKB. skbuff.c's __get_netmem and __put_netmem are the per-fragment refcounting hooks that know how to take and drop references on a devmem net_iov (which uses percpu_ref on the binding) versus a normal page. skb_pp_cow_data is the escape hatch: when something tries to read fragment bytes that the CPU cannot access (because they live on the GPU), it linearizes by copying into host pages.
tour.languageLesson: Devmem fragments are flagged unreadable. Any code path that calls skb_copy_bits or otherwise touches fragment payload must first cow the SKB, ensuring that legacy consumers (e.g., iptables, packet sockets) keep working even when the data plane uses device memory.

tour.title: Returning Tokens: SO_DEVMEM_DONTNEED
tour.description: Userspace receives devmem data as opaque tokens (offset + length into the dmabuf) via cmsg, then must tell the kernel when it's done so the underlying net_iov chunks can be freed back to the gen_pool. sock_devmem_dontneed implements the SO_DEVMEM_DONTNEED setsockopt: it parses an array of token ranges and drops the matching references. Without this, devmem leaks until the socket closes.
tour.languageLesson: SO_DEVMEM_DONTNEED is the RX-side completion mechanism for zero-copy: the kernel cannot reclaim a chunk while userspace might still be reading it via the GPU, so ownership is explicit. This mirrors the MSG_ZEROCOPY pattern on TX.

tour.title: Devmem TX via SCM_DEVMEM_DMABUF
tour.description: The TX direction is symmetric. __sock_cmsg_send parses sendmsg() ancillary control messages, including SCM_DEVMEM_DMABUF, which tags an outgoing skb with a dmabuf binding id and offset. The result is a TX skb whose fragments point directly at device memory, so the NIC can DMA from the GPU without an intervening copy.
tour.languageLesson: cmsg (SCM_*) is the socket layer's ancillary-data sideband. Each cmsg is a TLV inside the msghdr's control buffer, allowing per-sendmsg metadata (credentials, timestamps, devmem tokens) without polluting the data stream.

tour.title: Introspection: page_pool Stats Dump
tour.description: Operators need to see which page_pools exist and which carry a memory provider. netdev_nl_page_pool_get_dumpit walks the per-netdev page_pool registry and streams stats back over generic netlink, including the memory-provider info that identifies devmem-backed pools. This is how 'ethtool'-like userspace tools learn that a queue is devmem-bound.
tour.languageLesson: genl dumpit handlers are restartable: they receive a netlink_callback with cb->args[] for pagination state, allowing them to emit one chunk per kernel->userspace round-trip and resume mid-dump if the userspace buffer fills.

tour.title: Teardown & Lifecycle
tour.description: Closing the loop: net_devmem_unbind_dmabuf reverses Step 4, erasing the xarray entry that tracks the per-queue install, synchronizing with in-flight allocations, and dropping the binding's percpu_ref. netdev_nl_sock_priv_destroy is the safety net invoked when the userspace genl socket closes unexpectedly: it walks every binding owned by that socket and unbinds them, guaranteeing that a crashed userspace cannot strand device memory.
tour.languageLesson: percpu_ref is a scalable reference count with two phases: per-CPU counters during normal operation, then a kill+drain phase that converts to atomic counting and waits for all references to drop. This pattern is ubiquitous for kernel objects whose hot path must avoid atomic contention.
